map.Review: Fractions & Decimals — part of T: Review: Fractions & Decimals. This is part of The Pattern Engine arc. ½-benchmark fractions · add/subtract decimals. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It does not stop you.
map.Episode 1. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 1. Same crew. Same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are set.
map.That dome! The door's propped open — GO: Look, a dome! The door is open. GO GO GO!
map.Vexhall Observatory? Sealed since foreve: Vexhall? It has been shut for a long time. It is so spooky.
map.I'm Maya — that's Theo, Zara, and Dev. W: I'm Maya. That's Theo, Zara, and Dev. We are friends. We are wet, too.
I know. Book people know a lot. I'm Ms. Ortiz. Welcome to Vexhall.
map.Vexhall Observatory — built by Ada Vex,: This is Vexhall. Ada Vex built it. She was good at math. She made half of Axiom City. Then she went away. No one knows where.
map.Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand bo: Inside: brass, dust, and ten thousand books.
map.Ada Vex's last journal. Sealed sixty yea: Ada Vex's last book. It was shut for sixty years. The clasp opens for the right fraction.
map.Three engravings — and one instruction:: It has three carved signs. It has one rule: "FEED ME THE ONE BELOW ONE-HALF."
map.Use a benchmark — test each fraction aga: Use a benchmark. Test each fraction with 1/2. Look at the top number. Is it more or less than half the bottom?
map.Uh… did the lamps just blink three times: Um… did the lamps just blink? Three times. Then nine. Then twenty-seven.
map.A benchmark is a friendly reference numb: A benchmark is a known number, like 1/2. Use it to test the rest.
map.Reader — you're the fifth crew member no: Reader, you are on the crew now. You make five. Give the clasp the right fraction.
map.The clasp offers 3/8, 5/9, 7/12 and dema: The clasp shows 3/8, 5/9, 7/12. It wants the one below one-half. Then it checks how you think. Tap one answer in each row.
map.Conceptual: compare each fraction to the: Conceptual: check each fraction with the benchmark 1/2. Look at the numerator. Is it less than HALF the denominator? Then the fraction is less than 1/2.
map.Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is: Procedural: half of 8 is 4. Half of 9 is 4.5. Half of 12 is 6. Check each numerator with that half. Clasp B: how far is 5/9 from 1/2? From 1?
map.Beneath the reading room. The journal's: Under the big book room. The map in the book points DOWN.
map.A door with a combination. Ada didn't tr: A door with a code. Ada did not trust keys, I guess.
map.Decimal dials. Easy to wreck if you don': These dials use decimals. Mind place value, or you break them.
map.Write 3.6 as 3.60 — give it a hundredths: Write 3.6 as 3.60. Now it has a hundredths digit. Add tenths to tenths. Add hundredths to hundredths.
map.The door is humming. Doors should NOT hu: The door hums. Doors should NOT hum.
map.A decimal names part of a whole by place: A decimal names part of a whole. It uses place value. 3.6 means 3 ones and 6 tenths. That is the same as 3.60.
map.Dial carefully, reader. This door has op: Dial with care, reader. This door is fussy.
map.Two decimal dials, one rule: \"Sum, then: Two dials. One rule: "Sum, then difference." Find 3.6 + 2.85. Find 12.5 − 4.75. Then the door opens.
map.Conceptual: decimals add and subtract li: Conceptual: add and subtract decimals like whole numbers. But first, line up each digit by place value. Give 3.6 a hundredths digit: 3.60.
map.Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85 — add hu: Procedural: Dial 1: 3.60 + 2.85. Add hundredths. Then tenths. Then ones. Dial 2: 12.50 − 4.75. You will need to regroup.
map.The full story — The Pattern Engine — is: The full story is The Pattern Engine. It glows at the city gate. — A.V.
map.completed Unit 1 · Episode 1: Benchmark: completed Unit 1 · Episode 1: Benchmark & Brass. It is in The Pattern Engine arc. Now they know ½-benchmark fractions. And add/subtract decimals.
map.Next up: the full anchor volume — The Pa: Next up: the full volume, The Pattern Engine.
map.A practice clasp offers 2/5 and 4/7, ask: A test clasp shows 2/5 and 4/7. It wants the one below 1/2.
map.Half of 5 is 2.5 — and 2 < 2.5, so 2/5 s: Half of 5 is 2.5. And 2 < 2.5. So 2/5 is below the benchmark.
map.Half of 7 is 3.5 — and 4 > 3.5, so 4/7 s: Half of 7 is 3.5. And 4 > 3.5. So 4/7 is above. Give it 2/5.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.What numerator makes ?/8 land exactly ON: Find the numerator. It puts ?/8 right ON the 1/2 benchmark.
map.Write 2.4 as 2.40 so the hundredths line: Write 2.4 as 2.40. Now the hundredths line up: 2.40 + 1.35.
map.Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths: Add by place: 0+5 hundredths, 4+3 tenths, 2+1 ones → 3.75. The dial turns.
map.Both clasps need a choice — tap one butt: Both clasps need an answer. Tap one button in each row.
map.Clasp A stays shut. Test your pick: is i: Clasp A stays shut. Look at the numerator. Is it more or less than half its denominator?
map.Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is only a sliver: Clasp B stays shut. 5/9 is just a bit above 1/2. Check both distances first.
map.3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4), and 5/9 hu: 3/8 < 1/2 (3 is less than 4). And 5/9 is close to the 1/2 benchmark. The clasp pops open!
map.6.45 and 7.75 — the dials clack, the bra: 6.45 and 7.75. The dials click. The brass door rolls back!
map.A dial sticks. Line up the decimal point: A dial sticks. Line up the decimal points. Put tenths under tenths. Then go place by place.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
